title: The Grateful Dead Live at Saenger Performing Arts Center on 1982-09-09

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a wild ’82 show with a killer Uncle John’s Band → Samson → Uncle John’s sequence, standout Althea and Eyes, despite an abrupt first‑set stop.
ai_review.review: The recording is a high‑quality soundboard that delivers crisp mix and lets Phil’s bass roar, though a few audience patches and missing encore bits are noted. Musically the night was memorable – the first set ends abruptly when Weir quits the stage, but the second set rolls on nonstop with a sweet Althea jam, an explosive Uncle John’s Band‑Samson‑UJB sandwich, and a soaring Eyes that lifts the whole show.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars, praising both performance (high energy, standout songs) and recording (crisp soundboard). Minor complaints about missing sections and a few rough moments keep the rating just below the top tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with strong bass presence; occasional audience patches and missing encore sections, but overall excellent clarity for an ’82 board.

standout_songs: Uncle John's Band > Samson > Uncle John's Band
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set stops abruptly when Weir leaves the stage; second set opens with a surprising UJB‑Samson‑UJB sandwich and then flows nonstop, delivering high energy through Eyes into Good Lovin'.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Delivers sweet, muscular lead after Weir quits; standout work on Althea and a beautiful solo on Eyes.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass comes through like ‘the beast’, highlighted as a key strength of this board recording.
band_member_comments.Bob: Forgot lyrics on The Other One and bailed a bit on Althea, but regains eloquence on Good Lovin'.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (keyboards) joins the post‑Weir jam on Althea, adding to the sweet groove.
